[session compacted: the 163 earliest messages were replaced by the summary below; the 180 most recent messages after it are verbatim.]

---

# Session state

## The job

Issue **#476** (Japanese): on a root issue's aggregation re-entry, the machinery could not open the delivery pull request. Reported behaviour: `create_pr` resolved its head from the run's checkout (`main`), so `gh pr create` refused with `head branch "main" is the same as base branch "main"`. `sync_branch` refused too (`Cannot synchronize 'atomaton/issue-441' while 'main' is checked out`), and no tool switches checkout. Suggested directions were (a) check out the node's aggregation branch at run start, (b) let `sync_branch` act on a named branch, (c) add a head fallback in `create_pr`.

## What was diagnosed

I traced it further back than the issue did. The run never reached the aggregation branch at all, and the cause is in `src/adapters/github/issue-branches.ts`:

- `collectIssueBranches` asked "did any pull request from this branch **name** merge" (`parsed.some(pr => Boolean(pr.merged_at))`).
- A branch name outlives the pull requests from it. `atomaton/issue-441` was created by the first child's commit and kept receiving child merges; an earlier PR (#455) from the same name had already merged.
- So the tip `d9894f0`, carrying three undelivered merges, read as `merged: true`.
- `ordinalToResume` (in `src/domain/work/issue-branch.ts`) then answered "nothing to resume", `resolve_issue_branch.ts` wrote `branch=""`, and the runner checked out `main`.
- `create_pr` then had head == base, and refused.

So the fix belongs in the merge judgement, not in `create_pr`/`sync_branch`/`launch_sub_agent` — I deliberately did **not** implement options (b) or (c) from the issue.

## What was implemented and merged (PR #478, merged as `65ec6f3`, main is now `f2c5941`)

- `src/adapters/github/issue-branches.ts`: `collectIssueBranches` now carries `object.sha` from the same `git/matching-refs` response; `headBranchMerged(repo, owner, branch, tip)` returns true only when a merged PR's `head.sha === tip`. A failed/absent read answers **unmerged** (deliberate direction: resuming a branch with nothing new costs a run; calling undelivered work delivered loses it).
- `src/adapters/adapters.test.ts`: updated fixtures to carry `object.sha`; added regression test *"a branch that moved on after a merged pull request is not merged"*.
- `src/entrypoints/machinery/resolve_issue_branch.test.ts`: **new file** (the script had no test at all, which is why this survived). Five tests.
- `src/domain/work/issue-branch.ts`: `OwnedBranch.merged` doc comment reworded.
- `docs/work/how-it-works/the-branch-a-run-commits-to.md`: the resume rule now states the tip-based meaning.

Verified: both regression tests confirmed to fail on the unfixed code and pass with it; full `bun run test` = **2223 pass, 0 fail**; `typecheck`/`synth`/`scan_secrets` exit 0. Re-confirmed after merge on the merged tree: 2223 pass, 61 pass across the two focused files.

## OPEN — a regression my own fix introduces, not yet fixed

This is the live problem. My rule asks `merged_at && head.sha === tip`, but there is a second shape where the tip legitimately differs from `head.sha`: **when `atomaton/issue-N` is a parent branch that a child's PR merged *into*.** Then the tip is the merge commit created on that branch, not the head of any PR *from* it.

Real data gathered this run:

- `atomaton/issue-418`, tip `7f6ce01206d8ba1d17e2090777bfac1c17be5853`.
- PR #419 has `headRefName: atomaton/issue-418`, `baseRefName: atomaton/issue-12`, `head.sha = 87e54a9ba694a09969abab7bf5cf34031a7f9662`, `merge_commit_sha = 7f6ce012…`.
- So the tip **is** the merge commit → also compare against `merge_commit_sha`, not just `head.sha`.
- Confirmed already in main: `compare(main...7f6ce012…)` returned `merge_base_commit.sha = 7f6ce012…`.

Other real tips for reference: `atomaton/issue-12` `f4177a5…`, `atomaton/issue-164` `2f19723…`, `atomaton/issue-441` is now **deleted** (`matching-refs/heads/atomaton/issue-441` returns `[]`; PR #477 merged it to main at `f2c5941`).

The intended next change: make the merged test succeed when a merged PR's `head.sha` **or** `merge_commit_sha` equals the tip, and add a regression test for the parent-branch shape (PR merged *from* the branch's own tip when that tip is the merge commit of a PR *into* it). Then full validation, commit, and open the next PR — the issue stays open because this is a follow-on defect.

## Verified against real incident values

Running the delivered `resolve_issue_branch.ts` with the real `#441` values (tip `d9894f0…`, PR #455 head `1f208277…`) yields `branch="atomaton/issue-441"`, `resuming atomaton/issue-441` — i.e. the #476 fix works. A control where the PR had landed the tip answers `""`.

## Things a continuing run must not redo or forget

- Do **not** re-litigate the direction of the fix (options b/c in the issue were considered and rejected; the defect is upstream in the merge judgement).
- Do **not** edit `.github/atomaton-runtime/**` or `.github/workflows/**` — generated. Note that `.github/atomaton-runtime/scripts/resolve_issue_branch.ts:75` still contains the **old** logic; that is expected (it is the last release, `v0.21.58`, applied by self-deploy, not by a work PR).
- Do **not** touch `package.json` `version`.
- `.github/**` and `self/**` are governed paths — no agent merges changes there.
- Test seam: `ATOMATON_FAKE_GH` + `FAKE_GH_RESPONSES` rules match when **every** string in `match` is a substring of some argv element. `src/entrypoints/machinery/testing/harness.ts` exports `runWithFakeGh`, `scriptPath`, `parseGithubOutput`, `makeConfigDir`, `importable`, `hermeticEnv`. `src/adapters/adapters.test.ts` uses `makeShim` + the same harness.
- Shell guard blocks raw `git fetch`/`git push`/`gh` — use the GitHub tools. Reading API data is done with `fetch` (rate limits hit intermittently; `get_pr`, `get_branch`, `get_issue` are alternatives).
- A `delegate` sub-run for docs reading failed with `402 Payment Required / free_quota_exhausted` — the delegate pool has no model quota; do work inline rather than relying on delegates.
- Clean worktree at the start of the re-entry; scratch files were written to `/tmp/atomaton-workspace/` and deleted.

## Editing patterns established in this run

The document style is long-form prose comments stating *why*, with em-dashes and references to the shape of the failure — not restated code. Tests state the *behaviour* in the words of the requirement. Keep diffs minimal and delete rather than add where possible.

content.text:
Wait — there's a subtlety. `nextOrdinal` is used at the first commit to name a new branch. If a branch's name is reused (as the docs say: a merge deletes the branch, so the same name is free again), and the "merged" flag now depends on a tip match, then after a merge the branch would usually be deleted, so there'd be no branch to list at all.

But there's an important case: `branchForCommit` uses `nextOrdinal`. If a branch is merged but not deleted (deletion failed), the tip equals the merge's head.sha? Hmm, not necessarily — a merge commit on the base doesn't move the branch. The branch still points at its pre-merge tip. And `head.sha` of the merged PR equals that pre-merge tip (for a merge commit merge). So merged = true. Good — that keeps the "count up instead of reusing a merged branch" rule intact.

Now, the case from the issue: PR #455 merged *from* `atomaton/issue-441` into `main` with head sha `1f20827...` (per statuses_url of PR 455). Then children continued to merge into `atomaton/issue-441`, moving its tip to `d9894f0`. So head.sha (1f20827) != tip (d9894f0), so merged=false → resume the branch. Exactly right.

But wait: an important caveat. What if the tip *has* merged and the branch was not deleted, and then children merge into it? That's the case above. Fine.

Another caveat: what if the branch's tip is merged into the parent (for a sub-issue branch, a merge into a parent's branch)? Then merged = true and the run doesn't resume it. Right.

Another caveat: what if a PR is merged and the branch later gets a new commit from... nothing else. Fine.

Now consider: is `merged` used anywhere else where tip-matching would change behavior wrongly? `branchForCommit` → `nextOrdinal` only. `resumableBranch` → `ordinalToResume`. Both correct with the new semantics.

Hmm, but one more scenario for nextOrdinal: a branch merged and deleted, so not listed. Normally none. If a branch merged with PR (tip matches) → nextOrdinal counts up. Same as before.

Edge: what if a PR was merged from a branch and GitHub's `head.sha` doesn't match because the merge was performed after more pushes to the branch (so PR head sha is stale relative to branch tip)? Actually GitHub PR `head.sha` is the PR's current head, which tracks branch tip. After merge it's frozen at the merged commit. If work was pushed to the branch after merge, tip moves and head.sha stays → not merged → resume. Correct.

Now what about the other half of the defect: even after resuming `atomaton/issue-441`, would create_pr work? create_pr resolves branch = checked out branch. The runner's "Check out the branch this run starts from" step does `git fetch origin refs/heads/BRANCH:refs/remotes/origin/BRANCH` and `git checkout -B BRANCH refs/remotes/origin/BRANCH`, and sets `BRANCH=BRANCH` in GITHUB_ENV. Then create_pr: base = stackedPrBase(REPO) ?? getBaseBranch(). For root issue #441, stackedPrBase returns undefined (no parent) → base = getBaseBranch() = "" (config base_branch empty) → gh uses default branch main. head = branch = atomaton/issue-441. That works. And remote sha == HEAD because we just checked out origin/branch. 

But: is the head equals base refusal also possible if resolve_issue_branch still returns ""? With tip-matching merged, for #441 it returns atomaton/issue-441. Good.

Now — a second consideration. Should I also fix `sync_branch`/`create_pr` per the issue's suggested options (b)/(c)? The issue lists three candidate directions and asks the outcome: the parent's aggregation re-entry should be able to open the delivery PR from the integration branch. The root cause is (a)-adjacent: the run should be checked out on the node's aggregation branch, but resolve_issue_branch wrongly concluded there was nothing to resume. Fixing the premise makes (b) and (c) unnecessary. Minimal change is better. But is the fix robust? Consider: what if the aggregation branch has merged (delivered) and the parent is still open with nothing to do? Then merged=true, resume → "" → run on main, and create_pr isn't needed. Fine.

Consider: what if the parent's integration branch does NOT exist (children never committed) and the parent's run wants to deliver? Nothing to deliver. Fine.

Consider a case where the parent's branch tip is merged into main but not deleted, and the parent has no more work: merged=true → base. Good.

But there's another failure mode worth checking: after resuming, `create_pr` requires remote sha == local HEAD. The workflow checks out origin/branch so equal. Good.

Also: what about `git fetch origin` in the step — shallow clone fetch of a specific ref with actions/checkout fetch-depth 1 works (the workflow does this for issue branches already, that path has traffic).

Hmm, but the earlier report said `git cat-file -t d9894f0` failed in the run because the clone was shallow and the branch wasn't fetched. With the runner step doing the fetch, that's handled.

Now, is there anything else blocking? Let me think about `stackedPrBase` for the *parent* run: parent issue #441 has no parent → undefined → base main. Good.

One more concern: after resuming the aggregation branch and creating the delivery PR, `create_pr`'s dispatchPrValidation is fine.

Also, what about the `merged` flag semantics in the *sub-issue* case with `deletedMergedBranch`? merge_pr deletes the merged branch. Fine.

Now let me consider whether tip-matching is achievable: does `git/matching-refs/heads/<prefix>` return `object.sha`? Yes — the git refs API returns `{ref, node_id, url, object: {sha, type, url}}`. I couldn't fetch it live due to rate limits. Hmm. I should verify. Let me check the API docs from memory: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/matching-refs/{ref} returns an array of git ref objects: `{"ref": "refs/heads/feature-a", "node_id": "...", "url": "...", "object": {"type": "commit", "sha": "...", "url": "..."}}`. Yes, that's documented. But I should verify rather than assume, since the whole fix depends on it. Rate limited on web fetch... Maybe I can check via the `github` tools? get_branch gives sha for an exact branch, not matching-refs.

Alternative that avoids depending on object.sha: compare with `compare` API for containment. But that costs one call per branch and has the same "is this tip in the base" semantics... Actually a cleaner and cheaper approach: instead of tip equality, ask whether the PR's merged `head.sha` equals the current tip. That needs the tip. Or ask GitHub `compare/{base}...{branch}` status → `identical`/`behind` means contained. But base here would be the default branch... config base_branch. Hmm, more complexity.

Let me try to verify the matching-refs response shape. Maybe use an alternate route: `fetch` with a different unauthenticated endpoint later; rate limit 403 probably due to shared IP. Let me try api.github.com once more later. Or check if there's any fixture in the repo showing matching-refs output with object.sha — plan_deploy.test.ts uses matching-refs/tags with jq. In git-tags.ts they run `--jq '.[] | "\(.ref) \(.object.sha)"'` on `git/matching-refs/tags`, which proves the shape exists for tags and is the same endpoint family. That's strong evidence within the repo: `repos/${repo}/git/matching-refs/tags` with `.[] | ... .object.sha`. matching-refs is one endpoint with a ref prefix; `matching-refs/heads/atomaton/issue-12` is the same. So object.sha is available. Good — that's a checkable anchor: src/adapters/github/git-tags.ts:50.

However, safer still: what if `object` is absent (older fixture/enterprise)? Then tip = "" and no PR matches → merged=false → resume. That's the safe direction (resume rather than lose work), consistent with the documented direction. And a branch that's actually merged-and-left-behind would then be resumed and a new PR opened... Hmm, that could resurrect delivered work. But with object missing only in odd environments. Actually wait — that's a real risk: the existing test fixtures for collectIssueBranches use `JSON.stringify([{ ref: "refs/heads/atomaton/issue-12" }])` with no object — those tests will now report merged:false for issue-12 where they expected true. I need to update those tests (they're fixtures, and updating them to carry object.sha is correct: real API returns it).

But then in production: if object is missing → resume a merged branch. Consider "merged but deletion failed" case: the branch is listed, tip is not in base. Under old rule, merged=true → nextOrdinal → new name. Under new rule with missing object → merged=false → resume the merged branch → commit onto history that already merged → PR from it into base would show only the new commits? Actually a PR from a branch whose earlier commits are in main shows only the delta, which is fine-ish, but docs say "Work never resumes on merged history". So the failure is a documented-rule regression in a degraded environment.

Better: make the reader say whether the tip is known, i.e. fail closed toward the old behaviour when object.sha is absent? Which direction is worse? Let me think about what data actually exists: real API always includes object.sha. Absence would be a corrupted/partial response. Hmm.

Alternatively, avoid needing the tip's sha: instead of comparing head.sha to tip, ask `compare` for containment of the tip in the base branch. `isContained(repo, branch, commit)` exists in git-tags.ts and answers whether commit is in branch, using compare status. Semantics: "is this branch's tip already in the base?" That's precisely "the branch's work has landed". But the base for a sub-issue branch is the parent branch, not the default branch. `headBranchMerged` currently doesn't know the base. For a sub-issue branch merged into the parent's branch, containment in `main` would be false → merged=false → resume the child branch even though its PR merged into the parent. That would be wrong for sub-issues (it would make child runs resume branches that already merged into the parent, and default a PR base... actually create_pr's base = parent's branch which still exists; a sub-issue re-entry after merge would resume the merged child branch and open a second PR from it into the parent's branch, showing nothing new, or worse).

So containment-in-base is not the answer; the PR-based question is the right one, and the tip is how to date it. Since PR list already gives us `head.sha` per PR, and the ref list gives `object.sha`, tip equality is precise for both parent and child merges.

For the degraded case (no object.sha), I'll treat the tip as unknown and ask a second question that is safe: if the branch has a merged pull request AND we cannot tell the tip, keep the old answer (merged). Hmm, but that's the bug's behaviour in the case that matters... no wait, in the #441 case the object.sha IS available. The degraded path only exists if GitHub's response changes shape. Choosing old behaviour there = "work can be lost in a broken environment" (the bug returns), choosing resume = "delivered work may be resumed". 

Hmm, actually thinking again: what if object is missing → tip unknown. I could instead read the tip per branch with `readOriginBranch(branch)` (ls-remote) — the repo already has that in branch-reads.ts, one call per branch. But that's more calls. Simpler and honest: require the tip; if a listed ref has no `object.sha`, return `known: false` for the whole read with a why, because the list is not something we can use. That's the pattern this module already established ("says whether it knows"), and both callers handle unknown: resolve_issue_branch stays on base (safe, no branch created), branchForCommit throws with a message (won't create a name blind). In the broken-environment case that means a run stays on the base and resumes nothing — same as today's #441 outcome but reported, and the run can't lose work silently... Actually staying on base = can't deliver = the #476 bug, but loudly (log WARN).

Hmm. Which is best? An unread list already means "stay on base" for resolve_issue_branch. Adding "tip missing → unknown read" is consistent and simple, one rule instead of two. And the API does return object.sha, so this is a guard against a shape change, not a live path.

Let me reconsider simplicity: is there a way to avoid the tip entirely? The old code asked merged by name. What if instead we ask "does this branch have a merged PR *and* has the branch moved since"? Equivalent to tip comparison. Or: ask for the PRs with `state=open` first — if there's an *open* PR from this branch, it's not merged → resume. In the #441 case, when the parent re-entry run starts, is there an open PR from atomaton/issue-441? No — PR #455 was merged; the human's PR #477 exists only later. Children's PRs were from child branches. So "open PR exists" wouldn't have saved it.

What about counting merges into the branch versus... no.

Another angle: the real intent of "merged" is "this branch has no undelivered work", i.e. the branch's tip is contained in the branch it delivers to. For a child: parent branch. For a root: base. That's actually a cleaner definition and doesn't need PRs at all — but it needs the base branch and one compare call per branch, and requires the parent-vs-base distinction (parentIssueOf, which is a GraphQL call). More machinery.

The tip-equality fix is small, precise, and preserves the existing structure. I'll go with it, and return `known: false` when a listed ref carries no sha (with a `why`), because the merged flag cannot be computed without it.

Hmm, wait. Actually there's a subtlety with tip equality: after `merge_pr` merges a PR with `--merge` and deletes the branch, fine. But what about a *squash*? Ruleset pins merge commits. And a person merging via UI with merge commit → head.sha = branch tip at merge. Good.

Another subtlety: a merged PR whose head.sha equals the current tip, but the branch then received more commits that were later reverted? Irrelevant.

Another: a *closed-unmerged* PR from this branch and a later merged one — `some()` over merged ones handles it.

Another: the same branch name reused by an entirely different unit of work — e.g. branch merged into main, deleted, then a new branch created with the same name from the base (docs say a merge deletes the branch so the same name is free). New tip ≠ old PR head sha → merged=false → resume. Correct! Under the old rule, the new branch would be wrongly considered merged (the old PR is in the history of that name) and the run would refuse to resume it and count up a new ordinal. So this fix also repairs that case. Good, and it's a genuine second bug the same root cause explains. That's worth a test.

Now let me also consider whether resolve_issue_branch is enough, or whether the aggregation re-entry needs anything else. Let's re-read the issue's desired behaviour: "ルート issue の集約 re-entry では、launch_sub_agent が作った集約ブランチ(atomaton/issue-441)を head として create_pr できること". With the resume fix, the run is checked out on atomaton/issue-441 at start, BRANCH env set, create_pr heads it. So yes.

But one more thing: the workflow step "Check out the branch this run starts from" only sets BRANCH when resuming. It does `git checkout -B BRANCH refs/remotes/origin/BRANCH`. So HEAD == remote tip. create_pr then requires remote.sha == local HEAD: equal. Good.

Then create_pr: `git status --porcelain` — the machinery was moved out, so clean. Good.

Now, what about `commit_and_push`? Not needed; the delivery PR is opened with no new commits. create_pr doesn't require new commits. Good.

Let me now write the code, tests, and docs.

Let me first fix my edit: handle missing sha → known:false. Let me restructure the parse.

Also the variable name `refs_` is ugly (shadowing `refs`). Better: rename the gh result to `listed` and the array to `refs`. Let me rewrite the function cleanly.

content.text:
Now, `tip` being empty (`object` missing) — what does that do? `pr.head?.sha === tip` with `tip === ""` would be false always, so merged=false, which makes it resumable. That's the safe direction per the doc comment. But: is `object.sha` present on `matching-refs` for heads? The tags version uses `object.sha`. For `git/matching-refs/heads/...`, the GitHub API returns git refs objects with `object: {sha, type, url}`. Yes, same ref object shape.

However there's a subtlety: a merged PR's head sha vs. the branch tip — when a PR merges, the branch is usually deleted. But here the parent branch is not deleted (merge_pr's deleteMergedBranch runs... wait, PR #455 was merged by... let's see, from the record, was it merged by merge_pr? PR#455 merged, and branch atomaton/issue-441 still exists. Hmm, `deleteMergedBranch(headRefName)` is called on merge_pr. But the branch still exists — maybe because it was merged by a person, or the delete failed, or the branch received new pushes after the merge... Actually after #455 merged into main, the children then merged INTO atomaton/issue-441 again, recreating/pushing to the branch.

Hmm important: an important consideration — is `head.sha` of a merged PR preserved? For a merged PR, `head.sha` is the last commit of the head branch. Yes.

But careful: in this repo the parent branch is created by `stackedBaseFor` and children merge into it. PR #455 was a root-issue PR from atomaton/issue-441 into main — that was for §3 work merged earlier. Then later children (#460, #461, #462) merged into atomaton/issue-441, moving its tip to d9894f0. So `head.sha` of #455 was some earlier commit → merged=false now → resumable → the run checks out atomaton/issue-441. 

But wait — there's a wrinkle: the current checkout of the run is the base branch and `resolve_issue_branch` is what names the branch. Good.

Second wrinkle: does this affect the "ordinalToResume" semantics for the *merged* case where the branch was deleted? A deleted branch isn't listed, so irrelevant.

Third: what about a PR that merged with squash? `head.sha` still the last head commit. Fine. But then the branch tip equals that sha even though work went to base as a new commit — merged=true is still right (work landed). Good.

Fourth: an open (unmerged) PR from the tip → `merged_at` null → merged=false → resumable → correct.

Fifth: a *closed without merging* PR from the tip → merged false → resumable → correct.

Sixth: what about a branch whose tip commit equals a merged PR's head.sha but new commits were force-pushed... not relevant.

Now — a case that this changes and might be a regression: previously, a branch that had ANY merged PR was treated as merged. Now, if a merged PR exists whose head.sha equals the branch tip, merged=true — same as before in the ordinary case (branch merged and then deleted; but if the branch survived a failed deletion, tip == head.sha of merged PR → merged=true → nextOrdinal counts up). That's exactly the documented case in `the-branch-a-run-commits-to.md`: "If a merged branch is still there — a deletion that failed, or a merge made some other way — the next name counts up". Good, preserved, and now more precise.

The old test in adapters.test.ts: `head=owner:atomaton/issue-12` returns `[{merged_at: "..."}]` with no head.sha → now merged=false, so the existing test breaks. I need to update it to include head.sha matching the refs' object.sha. And the REFS fixture must include `object: {sha}`.

Let me now write the tests. Also should I handle this in a domain-pure way? The rule `ordinalToResume` is unchanged; only the input's `merged` flag is computed more precisely. That's the right place: the fact "this branch's work merged" belongs to the adapter reading GitHub.

Now, is the fix sufficient for the issue's desirable behaviour? The issue asks: in the root issue's aggregation re-entry, create_pr should be able to use the integration branch as head. With this fix, `resolve_issue_branch.ts` names `atomaton/issue-441`, and the runner's step checks it out and sets `BRANCH=atomaton/issue-441`. Then `create_pr` resolves head = BRANCH → correct; base = stackedPrBase (root, no parent) → main. Head ≠ base → PR opens. That satisfies (a) in the issue's proposal list and doesn't need (b)/(c).

But: `create_pr` also verifies remote sha === local HEAD. At the start of the run, HEAD is the tip of atomaton/issue-441 = d9894f0 which is on origin → equal → passes. Good.

Wait, but the run is an aggregation re-entry: the agent (atomaton) doesn't commit anything; the branch content already exists. create_pr requires clean worktree — yes. So it works.

One more consideration: after this fix, will a *non-aggregation* run on a root issue whose branch tip is undelivered wrongly resume the branch? Consider a run on issue X where X's branch has an open PR still under review. Then merged=false → resume → the run starts on that branch. That's already existing behaviour (unmerged branch is resumed). Fine.

Consider a run on a root issue whose branch has undelivered tip but the issue is sub-issue... same logic.

Consider: a normal work branch atomaton/issue-N whose PR merged into main. Tip sha equals the merged PR's head.sha → merged=true → not resumed (unless branch deleted). Same as before. 

Now consider the sub-issue scenario where the child's PR merged into the *parent's* branch: merged_at set, head.sha == tip → merged = true. Correct.

Now, an edge: PR head.sha for a closed-unmerged PR — `merged_at` null → false. Fine.

Now: a subtle one. Suppose the branch's tip was pushed, a PR opened from it, PR merged with merge commit, and then the branch got new commits, but the *same* PR's head.sha stays at the old commit — handled.

Another edge: what if the branch tip is behind... no.

Another important edge: shallow/`matching-refs` object sha for an annotated... branches don't have annotated refs. OK.

Now let's also double-check `IssueBranch` interface's `name` — fine.

Now consider whether `create_pr` should ALSO get a guard so this "head == base" refusal is legible. The issue mentions the confusion. But scope: leaf behaviour = the parent's aggregation re-entry can open the delivery PR. There's a second, smaller improvement: when create_pr's head resolves to the same branch as its base, the current error comes from gh with a confusing message. Should I add a refusal naming the cause? That would be a nicer failure, but is it requested? The issue's proposal list includes (c) "create_pr に node の集約ブランチがあればそれを head にする fallback". I chose (a) — the run starts on the aggregation branch. Rather than implementing (c) too (two answers to the same question — against the repo's stated taste), I should not.

But there's a real remaining gap worth considering: after the fix, if the branch tip differs from what the runner fetched... fine.

Hmm, but what about this scenario: the aggregation re-entry happens when the *last child's PR merges into the parent branch*. That merge sets the parent branch tip. Then dispatch_if_siblings_done dispatches the parent's atomaton run. At that moment the parent branch tip is fresh. resolve_issue_branch lists branches: atomaton/issue-441 tip = d9894f0, PRs from that head: #455 (merged, head sha old), plus children's PRs whose head branches were atomaton/issue-460 etc. — not matching head=atomaton/issue-441. # REST API endpoints for Git references

Use the REST API to interact with references in your Git database on GitHub

## [About Git references](#about-git-references)

A Git reference (`git ref`) is a file that contains a Git commit SHA-1 hash. When referring to a Git commit, you can use the Git reference, which is an easy-to-remember name, rather than the hash. The Git reference can be rewritten to point to a new commit. A branch is a Git reference that stores the new Git commit hash. These endpoints allow you to read and write [references](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-Git-References) to your Git database on GitHub.

## [List matching references](#list-matching-references)

Returns an array of references from your Git database that match the supplied name. The `:ref` in the URL must be formatted as `heads/<branch name>` for branches and `tags/<tag name>` for tags. If the `:ref` doesn't exist in the repository, but existing refs start with `:ref`, they will be returned as an array.

When you use this endpoint without providing a `:ref`, it will return an array of all the references from your Git database, including notes and stashes if they exist on the server. Anything in the namespace is returned, not just `heads` and `tags`.

Note

You need to explicitly [request a pull request](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#get-a-pull-request) to trigger a test merge commit, which checks the mergeability of pull requests. For more information, see "[Checking mergeability of pull requests](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/getting-started-with-the-git-database-api#checking-mergeability-of-pull-requests)".

If you request matching references for a branch named `feature` but the branch `feature` doesn't exist, the response can still include other matching head refs that start with the word `feature`, such as `featureA` and `featureB`.

### [Fine-grained access tokens for "List matching references"](#list-matching-references--fine-grained-access-tokens)

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

- [GitHub App user access tokens](/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-a-user-access-token-for-a-github-app)

- [GitHub App installation access tokens](/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-an-installation-access-token-for-a-github-app)

- [Fine-grained personal access tokens](/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens#creating-a-fine-grained-personal-access-token)

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

- "Contents" repository permissions (read)

This endpoint can be used without authentication or the aforementioned permissions if only public resources are requested.

{"title": "A branch is merged only when its current tip landed (#476)", "body": "## What was wrong

`collectIssueBranches` answered "did a pull request from this branch **name** merge", and that is not the same question as "is this branch's work in the base". A branch name outlives the pull requests from it: a parent issue's branch is created by the first child's commit and carries every child's merge, so a pull request from it can land — part of the tree reaching the base — while the branch goes on receiving work.

#441 is that shape. Three child merges sat on `atomaton/issue-441` at `d9894f0`, undelivered, and an earlier pull request from the same name had already merged. The oldest question answered `merged`, so `ordinalToResume` reported nothing to resume and the parent's aggregation run started on `main`. `create_pr` then resolved its head from the checkout, found it equal to its base, and refused:

```
head branch "main" is the same as base branch "main", cannot create a pull request
```

`sync_branch` could not help either — it acts on the branch actually checked out — so no tool could open the delivery pull request. A person merged it by hand.

## What this changes

**The tip is part of the question.** `collectIssueBranches` reads `object.sha` from the same `git/matching-refs` response it already made, and a merged pull request whose `head.sha` is some earlier commit says only that the branch has moved on since. #
# tag-release.sh — put the tag on, and nothing else.
#
# The first half of this project's own release, declared in `deploy.on_merge`.

# here — this repository shipped `on_tag` and never once used it, so the bug that

#
# So the tag is the trigger now. This creates it; the tag's own deployment publishes.
#
# ## What that costs, stated rather than hidden
#
# A window. Between this and a successful publish, the tag exists with no release
# behind it. The single script had no such window, and that was its best property.
#
# It is bounded and it is recoverable: the publish is idempotent, and re-running it
# is one dispatch —
#
#     gh workflow run atomaton-deploy.yml --ref "$TAG" -f target=publish
#
# What this script will not do is create the tag twice, so a failed publish is never
# hidden by the next merge quietly starting over.
#
# The version is not passed in. `package.json`'s `version` is the single declaration

#
# Idempotent, and that is what makes `on_merge` safe. This runs after every merge and
# stops immediately when the version already has a release.
set -euo pipefail

VERSION=$(jq -r '.version // empty' package.json)
if [ -z "$VERSION" ]; then
  echo "::error::package.json declares no version; nothing can be released."
  exit 1
fi

  echo "::error::package.json version '$VERSION' is not a plain semver string."

## What was wrong

A run the core filed `failed` that left no output posted **nothing at all**. The step it ran in succeeded — `atoma` exits with the status of a stop it handled — so "Report failure" never ran, and `post_result_comment.ts` skipped on the only evidence it had: the session's last assistant turn carried tool calls, read as proof that a session-ending tool had posted a comment instead. It had not.

#441's run ended on its context budget after `fetch, fetch`. No comment, no `atomaton:ended` tag, so the thread's guard stayed held, and a person learned what had happened only by opening the run and reading its log.

## What this changes

**The skip is inverted to evidence, not shape.** The `ending-comment.json` record a session-ending tool writes when it posts its own comment is now the one thing that says "this run already has an ending on the thread". Where it exists, the footer is appended onto that comment; where it does not, this script posts the ending itself. `endedWithToolCalls` is deleted together with its `describe` block — a session's shape cannot prove another component spoke, and #441 is the counter-example (its last turn was a real tool call whose tool posted nothing).

The direction of error is deliberate and worth a reviewer's attention: a duplicate comment is noise somebody reads past, while silence holds a thread's guard forever and lets it delete a person's later comments (#194, #186). Holding that guard on a guess about another component is the larger harm.

**`failed` joins the `cutShort` family** (`stopped|runtime|iterations|loop|failed`), which fixes three things at once: the mention wording, the escaping of `@names` in text that is not a call (`notACall`), and the salvage path. It is deliberately **not** a `reachedLimit` — a failure is not a ceiling, and the tool tally would explain the wrong thing. The mention gets its own sentence (`stopped mid-run, and no agent will run next. Resume it, or say what to do instead.`) because the cut-short template would build "did not finish before it finished". The footer's ⚠️ line is gated on `reachedLimit` rather than `cutShort`, so a failed run's footer does not repeat the notice printed above it.

**The notice is one spelling, in a new module.** `src/entrypoints/machinery/lib/failure-notice.ts` holds `logExcerpt`, `logExcerptFrom` and `failureLines({agent, excerpt, notify?, runUrl?})`. `report_run_failure.ts` and `post_result_comment.ts` both use it; two spellings of "what became of your run and what you can do next" would be two answers free to drift. `runUrl` is passed by the caller whose comment has no footer and omitted by the one whose footer already links the run, so one fact is not printed twice.

**The excerpt keeps the tail and counts warnings.** `INTERESTING` now includes `warn` and `slice(-5)` replaces `slice(0, 5)` — the only explanation #441's log offered was two WARN lines about the context budget, and the first five matching lines of a long log are start-up chatter.

**A failed run with salvaged text is labelled a fragment**, so the last sentence before a failure is never presented as a result.

## Behaviour, by case

| Ending | Output | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `failed` | empty, no record | failure notice posted, `atomaton:ended` tag, mention |
| `failed` | empty, record exists | footer appended onto the tool's comment (PATCH, no POST) |
| `failed` | text | notice + the text under the `salvaged` warning |
| `stopped`/limit, empty | — | unchanged: cut-short notice (existing contract tests keep passing) |
| no-report | empty | unchanged |

`src/entrypoints/machinery/post_result_comment.ts` no longer reads the session to decide whether to skip; it reads it only to salvage. `--logs-file` (already passed by the runner) supplies the excerpt. `docs/work/how-it-works/how-a-run-ends.md` gains the two ways a failed run reaches the notice and what the second one's absence cost; the comment above `"ending-comment"` in `atomaton-runner.wac.ts` now states that the record is the one evidence.

- `bun run typecheck` — exit 0
- `bun run test` (full, `pretest: synth` first) — **2191 pass, 0 fail**
- `bun test ./tests/contract` — 497 pass, 0 fail (includes the "no script opens the run's own files by a bare name" guard)
- `bun test ./src/entrypoints/machinery/post_result_comment.test.ts` — 71 pass, including the three script-level failed-run tests (posts despite a tool-call session shape and quotes the WARN line; labels leftover text a fragment; PATCHes the recorded ending comment instead) and the existing stopped/limit tests
- `bun test ./src/entrypoints/machinery/report_run_failure.test.ts` — 19 pass, including two new excerpt tests

## Scope

Let me check branch issue-12: branch tip f4177a59, PR #427 head 6759b195 — different. So under the old rule, the branch would read as merged even though it moved on. Under the new rule it reads unmerged → resumed. That's the fix working on real data.

But wait — there's a subtlety I must consider carefully. Is "the branch moved on after its PR merged" always meaning "undelivered work"? Consider: a merged PR from branch atomaton/issue-12 at sha X. Then the branch receives a NEW commit. That new commit is indeed undelivered work — unless the branch was force-pushed to the same content or the merge was a squash (in which case branch commits are re-created). Hmm, with squash merge, the branch's own commits are collapsed; the branch tip would remain at X typically. Then next run would... the branch is at X, PR merged at X → merged → new branch name counts up. That's the documented behaviour ("next name counts up instead").

Under the old rule: branch at any sha, PR merged → merged. New rule: only if tip == PR head sha.

So for issue-12: branch at f4177a59 but PR #427 head was 6759b195. So the branch moved on. Does that mean undelivered work, or a merge of main into the branch, or something else? Note PR #427 merged at 2026-11-03T13:00:07 — but the merge commit is 5c1dbb7 into main... but wait, that PR's base — issue-12 is the ROOT issue #12, so its PR targeted main and merged. But mergePr deletes the merged branch. Yet atomaton/issue-12 still exists at f4177a59.

Hmm, PR #427's merge_commit_sha is 5c1dbb7. So it merged. Then branch moved to f4177a59? That's possible if a later run committed to atomaton/issue-12 (name reused after deletion... no, it wasn't deleted since it exists).

Actually, deleteMergedBranch may have failed, or the PR was merged by a person through the web UI (not via merge_pr tool) so no deletion. Then the branch still at the merged head 6759b195... but it's at f4177a59, which is different.

This is a real question: is my change safe? If a branch exists at a sha that isn't its merged PR's head, the old code says merged (nothing to resume → stay on base, plan a new name via nextOrdinal). New code says unmerged → resume that branch.

Consequence of resuming such a branch: the run checks out a branch whose work is already in main. If the run then commits, it commits on top of history that includes already-merged commits — that's fine and git handles it; the branch would be behind main though, and the PR would need main merged in. Not catastrophic, but it does contradict the documented "Work never resumes on merged history."

But hold on. What actually makes a branch tip differ from a merged PR's head, in this repository's flow? The children of an issue merge INTO the parent's branch (`atomaton/issue-441`), by merge commits, via merge_pr. And merge_pr deletes the head branch only when... let me look. In mergePr: `deleteMergedBranch(headRefName)`. hmm, is that gated on base being default? Let me check. It looked unconditional at line 2158. But wait — docs said "Deployment is not dispatched for a merge into a parent branch", and `dispatchCd(baseRefName)` — there's probably a gate. Let me check whether deleteMergedBranch is called for a stacked merge (child → parent branch). If it deletes the CHILD's branch (`atomaton/issue-460`) after merging into `atomaton/issue-441`, then children's branches vanish and only the parent's remains. Yes.

So for issue-441 (the parent), its branch keeps receiving merge commits from children — the tip moves — while an earlier PR #455 from `atomaton/issue-441` to main had merged. Under old rule: merged at ANY tip = nothing resumable. That's the bug.

For issue-12: tip f4177a59 vs PR #427 head 6759b195. Branch moved on after PR #427 merged. Under new rule it's "unmerged" → a run on #12 would resume `atomaton/issue-12`. Is that right or wrong? It's the same class as the documented case; and importantly #12 is a root issue whose branch got delivered and then received more work — but that more work is undelivered, which is exactly the intent.

Actually wait. Let me look more carefully at whether f4177a59 contains 6759b195 as ancestor, and whether it's just main's advances merged in. Either way, if the branch has commits not in main, resuming is right. Let me verify with the compare API: main...f4177a59 — if status is "ahead", the branch has undelivered commits. If "behind" or "identical", nothing to deliver and resuming is wrong (the next name should count up).

That's the real risk of my change: a branch whose tip is behind/identical to main but not equal to the merged PR's head would be resumed and a new branch would not be created. Hmm, but is that harmful? The run would checkout atomaton/issue-12 which equals an ancestor of main... then commit_and_push would push onto it and PR would show the merged commits again as new? No — if the branch is behind main, the PR base main already contains everything; the diff would be just the new commit. Git can compute that fine. So the PR would only carry the new work. Not harmful.

But it would mean the ordinal is reused rather than counted up, contradicting "Work never resumes on merged history" in the docs. That's a documented rule I'd be weakening. Hmm.

Let me think about whether a better rule exists that satisfies both:
- Rule: merged iff the branch's tip is contained in the base (nothing undelivered). That's `isContained` via compare API.
- My rule: merged iff some merged PR's head sha == tip.

Which is more correct for the purpose? Purpose is: "does this branch hold undelivered work?" The best answer is ancestry: is the tip contained in base. But an ancestry walk was deliberately rejected because squash/rebase rewrite commits — with a squash merge, the branch tip would NOT be in main even though its work is delivered. Hmm, but this repo pins merge commits. Still, issue-branches.ts explicitly explains why ancestry was rejected.

Hmm, careful. Let's re-read that comment: "Merged is read from the pull requests rather than from git ancestry: neither of the two rewritten merge methods leaves ancestry to follow... so a branch whose work is in the base would still look unmerged, and a run that believed that would resume a branch whose commits are already released."

So the existing design chose PR-based to avoid resuming released branches. My change makes "resume" more likely again for branches whose tip ≠ merged PR head. In the squash case, the tip after a squash merge stays the same as the PR head usually (branch not deleted → tip = merged head) → still reads merged. Good. So squash isn't affected much.

The case that changes: branch tip ≠ merged PR head. Two sub-cases:
(a) branch took more commits after a PR merged → undelivered work → resume is correct (new behaviour, the fix).
(b) branch was force-pushed / rebased to a different sha, or a person merged then the branch got a merge-from-main commit → tip differs but nothing undelivered conceptually. Resuming is wasteful but harmless.

Is (b) real here? For issue-12, tip f4177a59 vs PR head 6759b195. Hmm, note the PR #427 merge_commit_sha 5c1dbb7 which equals... and interestingly issue-164's branch is 2f19723; issue-418 branch tip 7f6ce012 which equals PR #419's merge_commit_sha! So for issue-418: branch tip 7f6ce012 == merge_commit_sha of PR #419, but PR #419's head sha was 87e54a9b. So the branch was reset/advanced to the merge commit in main. So under my new rule, issue-418 reads unmerged, whereas old read merged.

Hmm! That's case (b): after merging, something pushed the merge commit back onto the branch. Actually more likely: merge_base_into_branch? No... Let me think: PR #419 merged as 7f6ce012 into main. The branch atomaton/issue-418 now sits AT 7f6ce012, the merge commit that is already in main. So the branch's work is fully delivered; nothing undelivered. Under my rule: merged=false → a run on #418 would resume atomaton/issue-418 instead of starting a fresh atomaton/issue-418-2.

Is that harmful? The checkout would be at 7f6ce012 which is an ancestor of main (contained). Committing on it and pushing: PR diff vs main = only the new work. So functionally OK, but it contradicts "Work never resumes on merged history" and would break the documented ordinal count-up behaviour, and would leave a stale branch name in use.

Hmm. That's a real regression risk in behaviour, though benign in effect. Can I do better? Yes: a branch is merged if its tip is contained in the base OR a merged PR from it landed that exact tip. The "contained in base" test handles the (b) cases (branch reset to a merged commit / main's tip). And it handles squash merges? No — with squash, the branch commits aren't in base, so containment says not contained; then the exact-tip PR check says merged. Together they cover both.

But is containment cheap? One `compare` API call per branch: `repos/{repo}/compare/{base}...{branch}` → status. That's exactly `isContained` in git-tags.ts. So: merged = isContained(base, branch) || mergedPrAtTip.

Hmm, but that requires knowing the base branch inside collectIssueBranches, and adds an API call per branch. Complexity grows. Let me weigh.

Actually — wait. Let me reconsider. Is the simpler framing enough: what actually distinguishes #441's case is that the branch has commits that are NOT in main. Containment is exactly that question, and it's the semantically right one. The PR-head-sha check is a proxy for it. Given the repository already has `isContained` written for exactly this and documented as measured ("Measured against this repository: main...v0.1.157 answers behind"), using containment would be the cleaner rule and would keep the documented "never resume merged history" true in the (b) cases.

But: is containment reliable in the shallow clone? It's an API call (compare), not local git, so yes.

Cost: one extra API request per candidate branch. Candidates are few (usually 1). And it removes the need for the PR query entirely? If containment answers "behind/identical" → merged (delivered). If "ahead" → the branch has commits not in base → undelivered → not merged. If "diverged" → both have commits; branch has undelivered work → not merged. So containment ALONE answers the question, and better than the PR query, in this repo which uses merge commits only. But the comment explicitly says squash/rebase would break it — and this repo's ruleset pins merge-only, but adopters may not. An adopter with squash merging would get "ahead/diverged" forever after a squash merge → resume a released branch. That's the historical defect that PR-based reading fixed.

So the safest combination is: merged iff (contained in base) OR (a merged PR landed this exact tip). That's both signals, and neither alone.

Hmm, but this is now a bigger change than my merged PR. Am I over-engineering? Let me check: does the (b) case actually matter, i.e., does it cause a real problem? Under my current merged code, a run on an issue whose branch sits exactly at its own merge commit (issue-418) would resume that branch. Consequences: the oracle is a stale branch name being reused; the run starts on it; if it commits, the PR head is a branch that contains an already-merged commit; diff is fine. It also means `nextOrdinal` never counts up, so branch names never advance for such issues. Not fatal. But it *is* a behaviour the docs promise ("Work never resumes on merged history"), and I'd rather not leave a documented contradiction.

Let me verify with real data whether such a case exists and whether containment would resolve it. issue-418 tip 7f6ce012 = PR #419 merge_commit_sha, which is on main (it was merged into main? wait, base of PR #419 — let me check. issue-418 is a root issue presumably, so base main. merge_commit_sha 7f6ce012 — and PR #419 state closed merged. So 7f6ce012 is in main.) Let me confirm main contains it. `git` locally: is 7f6ce012 an ancestor of main? Let me check with ls-remote/compare API.

Also issue-12 tip f4177a59, PR #427 head 6759b195, merge_commit_sha 5c1dbb7. Is f4177a59 in main?

Let me measure these with the compare API. If both are contained in main, then in this repo there are exactly two stale leftovers of case (b), and my rule would resume deleted-work branches — a real, observable regression in behaviour on live data. That's worth fixing properly.

The purpose of the "merged" flag:
1. `ordinalToResume`: don't resume a branch whose work is already delivered. Resuming a delivered branch would build on history the base already contains.
2. `nextOrdinal`: when everything merged, count up the name.

The truth we want is "has this branch's work already reached the base?" That is exactly what `git-tags.ts`'s `isContained` asks: `repos/{repo}/compare/{branch}...{commit}` → `behind`/`identical` means contained; `diverged` or `ahead` means not.

So the right question for a branch tip: is the tip contained in the base branch? Compare base...tip:
- `behind`: tip is an ancestor of base → contained → merged/delivered.
- `identical`: tip == base → delivered.
- `ahead`: tip is ahead of base → NOT delivered → resume.
- `diverged`: tip has commits not in base → NOT delivered → resume.

That's the correct and simpler rule! And it handles:
- #441: tip d9894f0 vs main — d9894f0 is not in main (main has f2c5941 which merged it now, but at the time, d9894f0 was ahead/diverged) → not delivered → resume. ✓

## What was wrong

A run the core filed `failed` that left no output posted **nothing at all**. The step it ran in succeeded — `atoma` exits with the status of a stop it handled — so "Report failure" never ran, and `post_result_comment.ts` skipped on the only evidence it had: the session's last assistant turn carried tool calls, read as proof that a session-ending tool had posted a comment instead. It had not.

#441's run ended on its context budget after `fetch, fetch`. No comment, no `atomaton:ended` tag, so the thread's guard stayed held, and a person learned what had happened only by opening the run and reading its log.

## What this changes

**The skip is inverted to evidence, not shape.** The `ending-comment.json` record a session-ending tool writes when it posts its own comment is now the one thing that says "this run already has an ending on the thread". Where it exists, the footer is appended onto that comment; where it does not, this script posts the ending itself. `endedWithToolCalls` is deleted together with its `describe` block — a session's shape cannot prove another component spoke, and #441 is the counter-example (its last turn was a real tool call whose tool posted nothing).

The direction of error is deliberate and worth a reviewer's attention: a duplicate comment is noise somebody reads past, while silence holds a thread's guard forever and lets it delete a person's later comments (#194, #186). Holding that guard on a guess about another component is the larger harm.

**`failed` joins the `cutShort` family** (`stopped|runtime|iterations|loop|failed`), which fixes three things at once: the mention wording, the escaping of `@names` in text that is not a call (`notACall`), and the salvage path. It is deliberately **not** a `reachedLimit` — a failure is not a ceiling, and the tool tally would explain the wrong thing. The mention gets its own sentence (`stopped mid-run, and no agent will run next. Resume it, or say what to do instead.`) because the cut-short template would build "did not finish before it finished". The footer's ⚠️ line is gated on `reachedLimit` rather than `cutShort`, so a failed run's footer does not repeat the notice printed above it.

**The notice is one spelling, in a new module.** `src/entrypoints/machinery/lib/failure-notice.ts` holds `logExcerpt`, `logExcerptFrom` and `failureLines({agent, excerpt, notify?, runUrl?})`. `report_run_failure.ts` and `post_result_comment.ts` both use it; two spellings of "what became of your run and what you can do next" would be two answers free to drift. `runUrl` is passed by the caller whose comment has no footer and omitted by the one whose footer already links the run, so one fact is not printed twice.

**The excerpt keeps the tail and counts warnings.** `INTERESTING` now includes `warn` and `slice(-5)` replaces `slice(0, 5)` — the only explanation #441's log offered was two WARN lines about the context budget, and the first five matching lines of a long log are start-up chatter.

**A failed run with salvaged text is labelled a fragment**, so the last sentence before a failure is never presented as a result.

## Behaviour, by case

| Ending | Output | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `failed` | empty, no record | failure notice posted, `atomaton:ended` tag, mention |
| `failed` | empty, record exists | footer appended onto the tool's comment (PATCH, no POST) |
| `failed` | text | notice + the text under the `salvaged` warning |
| `stopped`/limit, empty | — | unchanged: cut-short notice (existing contract tests keep passing) |
| no-report | empty | unchanged |

`src/entrypoints/machinery/post_result_comment.ts` no longer reads the session to decide whether to skip; it reads it only to salvage. `--logs-file` (already passed by the runner) supplies the excerpt. `docs/work/how-it-works/how-a-run-ends.md` gains the two ways a failed run reaches the notice and what the second one's absence cost; the comment above `"ending-comment"` in `atomaton-runner.wac.ts` now states that the record is the one evidence.

## Verification

- `bun run typecheck` — exit 0
- `bun run test` (full, `pretest: synth` first) — **2191 pass, 0 fail**
- `bun test ./tests/contract` — 497 pass, 0 fail (includes the "no script opens the run's own files by a bare name" guard)
- `bun test ./src/entrypoints/machinery/post_result_comment.test.ts` — 71 pass, including the three script-level failed-run tests (posts despite a tool-call session shape and quotes the WARN line; labels leftover text a fragment; PATCHes the recorded ending comment instead) and the existing stopped/limit tests
- `bun test ./src/entrypoints/machinery/report_run_failure.test.ts` — 19 pass, including two new excerpt tests

## Scope

This is **§3 of the analysis on #441 only**. The session compaction defect (§1) and the ending names in the core (§2) live in `yuma-seno/atoma` and are out of scope here; so are the janitor (§4) and dispatch adoption (§5). A related core-side dependency: `post_result_comment`'s ARGS API is now parameterised — `--ended-because failed` has to arrive, and the workflow already passes it — but nothing in `atoma` itself changed in this PR.

`dist/` is gitignored and untouched. No version bump.

content.text:
These fetches are burning context. Let me stop and reason from what I have.

Key finding: My merged fix compares `pr.head.sha === tip`. But consider the *stacked* shape:

- Issue #418's branch `atomaton/issue-418` tip is `7f6ce01`, which is the MERGE COMMIT created when PR #419 merged. PR #419's head.sha is `87e54a9`. So `pr.head.sha (87e54a9) !== tip (7f6ce01)`.

Wait — but that merge was PR #419 merging INTO main, from branch atomaton/issue-418. And the compare shows `merge_base_commit: 7f6ce01` for `main...7f6ce01` — meaning 7f6ce01 is an ancestor of main. Actually compare(main...7f6ce01) with merge_base == 7f6ce01 means 7f6ce01 IS reachable from main. So the branch's work is delivered.

But my new rule would say: "is there a merged PR from this branch whose head.sha == tip (7f6ce01)?" PR #419's head was 87e54a9, not 7f6ce01. Merging #419 created merge commit 7f6ce01... 

Hmm wait. How did the branch tip become the merge commit? Because `merge_pr` for a PR merging into main... Actually no. Look: the commit 7f6ce01's message is "Merge pull request #419 from yuma-seno/atomaton/issue-418". A merge PR commit normally lands on the BASE branch (main). But the branch tip `atomaton/issue-418` points at 7f6ce01 too?

Actually `merge_pr` does `deleteMergedBranch(headRefName)` — deletes the head branch after merge. So the branch shouldn't exist. But it does exist at 7f6ce01.

Hmm, that's because after the merge, `merge_base_into_branch` or something... Actually more likely: the branch was left behind (deletion failed), and it was later fast-forwarded / or the branch is at a commit that includes the merge.

Wait — actually it could be that this branch was used again for a later piece of work. But the HEAD of atomaton/issue-418 = 7f6ce01 which is the merge commit from PR #419, which merged issue-418's branch into main.

Hmm, so if 7f6ce01 is on main AND is the branch tip... how? Actually a merge commit "Merge pull request #419 from ... atomaton/issue-418" has two parents: main's tip (a9e0058) and the branch head (87e54a9). That commit is on main. For the branch ref to be at 7f6ce01, something pushed main's content back onto the branch.

That's what `git checkout -B branch origin/branch` would... no.

OK — regardless of mechanism, the important thing: is `atomaton/issue-418` at a tip that is already in main? The compare says yes (merge_base = 7f6ce01). So resuming it would be wrong — work is already delivered. My new rule says "not merged" (because no merged PR has head.sha == 7f6ce01), so it would resume it and a run would start on an already-delivered branch.

That IS a regression: the old rule said "merged" (PR #419 from this branch merged) → don't resume. New rule says "unmerged" → resume.

Is that harmful? Per the docs: "Work never resumes on merged history." Resuming a delivered branch means the next run starts on a branch whose content is already in main. Then `commit_and_push` would push to it, `create_pr` would find head==base content... actually it'd create a PR from atomaton/issue-418 to main with no diff, which GitHub refuses or which is a no-op. Or worse, the run does new work on top of already-merged history and the PR carries only the new commits — that's actually mostly fine but it violates the stated rule and can produce an empty/odd PR.

Also: `branchForCommit` uses `nextOrdinal` only when nothing is resumable. If the branch is wrongly resumable, a NEW piece of work would go onto the old branch name instead of counting up to `-2`. That's the documented->merged-history problem.

So my fix trades one defect for another. I need to handle both:
1. Branch tip landed by a merged PR whose head.sha == tip → merged.
2. Branch tip is CONTAINED in the base branch → merged (regardless of which PR).

Actually the correct, complete question is: "is this branch's tip already in the base?" That's what `isContained(repo, base, tip)` answers — `behind` or `identical` means contained. That is exactly what the docs mean by "work never resumes on merged history."

But careful: for an in-progress branch that has NOT merged, compare(base...tip) = "ahead" or "diverged" → not contained → resume. Correct.

For #441: tip d9894f0 not in main → "ahead"/"diverged" → resume. Correct.
For #418: tip 7f6ce01 IS in main → "behind"/"identical" → merged. Correct.

And this removes the need for the PR-head comparison entirely — one question, answered by git containment, which is more direct than "did a PR from this name merge". Hmm, but there's a caveat the code documents: squash/rebase means ancestry doesn't follow. But this repo pins merge-commits only, and more importantly the containment question is asked of the RESULT (is the tip already in base), so squash would leave the tip NOT contained → resume a delivered branch. That's the documented reason for using merged_at.

So: the robust rule is "merged if (a) the tip is contained in the base, OR (b) a merged PR from this branch landed exactly this tip." Combining both covers:
- merge-commit method: containment catches it.
- squash/rebase method: PR head.sha == tip catches it.
- #418 (tip is a merge commit pushed back onto branch): containment catches it.
- #441 (tip not delivered): neither catches it → resume. Correct.

But that's more machinery and more API calls. Is it justified? The cost: one extra `compare` API call per branch. The alternative (only PR-head) regresses #418.

Hmm, wait. Let me reconsider. Is #418 actually going to be evaluated? resolve_issue_branch runs for issue 418 only when a run starts on issue 418. That's rare but possible. And the branches existing now (issue-12, issue-164, issue-418) are all delivered and would be wrongly resumable.

Actually, let me reconsider whether this even matters much: `ordinalToResume` picks the newest unmerged. If a stale delivered branch is wrongly "unmerged", then a new run on that issue resumes it instead of starting fresh from base. That's the documented-defect shape ("Work never resumes on merged history"), so yes it matters.

Let me just check: is `pr.head.sha === tip` ever true for these existing branches? For issue-12: tip f4177a5, PR #427 head 6759b19 → no. For issue-164: unknown. So all stale branches would flip to "unmerged". That's a real regression across the repo.

So I must fix it. The cleanest single question that answers the intent: **is the branch's tip already in the base branch?** Use `isContained`. And keep the PR-head check as the fallback for rewritten merge methods — actually, if I use containment plus PR-head-exact, that covers everything.

Hold on. Let me think about which is simpler and correct with least machinery.

Actually there's a simpler framing that's still one question: the tip is delivered if a merged PR from this branch has the tip as its head **or** the tip is an ancestor of the base. The second subsumes the first under merge commits. Under squash, only the first works.

Since this repo pins merge-only, and the general adopter may allow squash... the existing code's comment says merged_at was chosen precisely because rewritten methods break ancestry. So I should keep merged_at and ADD containment — but that's two questions.

Alternative: keep it as "merged_at AND head.sha === tip" and accept #418? No — that's a regression I introduced.

Hmm, but actually — wait. Is #418's shape even *produced* by Atomaton? The branch tip equals the merge commit that landed on main. That looks like `merge_base_into_branch`-related or a manual push. Let me not over-index. But the branch exists in this repo at exactly that shape, so it is reachable in practice.

Part of #418
Part of #418

## 何をするか

attachments サーバーに `fetch_attachment` を足す。Issue コメントに添付されたファイルを `/tmp` に保存し、開いて・編集して・`publish_draft` で送る流れの最初の部品。

- 引数: `url`（必須）、`filename`（任意）、`dir`（任意、既定 `/tmp/atomaton-workspace/attachments`）。
- 戻り値: `{ path, bytes, content_type, source_url }`。`bytes` は復号後の最終レスポンス本文のサイズ。
- ホスト allowlist: `https://github.com/user-attachments/...` と `https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/...` のみ。他は拒否。`http:` も拒否。
- リダイレクトは**同一呼び出し内で追跡**（`redirect: "follow"`）。#415 の実測どおり署名 URL は 5 分で切れるので、Location を返して 2 回目に取る形にはできない。
- 25MB 上限: `content-length` を見たうえで、**stream しながら**バイト数を数えて越えた時点で打ち切る（ヘッダは符号化後の長さなので、ヘッダが上限内でも本文が上限内とは限らない — #415 で 40 バイト宣言 / 復号 9 バイトを実測）。越えたら何も書かない（途中まで書かれたファイルは完全なものと区別できない）。
- トークンは送らない（`Authorization` を付ける引数も無い）。public asset では受理と無視が同一応答なので観測できるものが無い、という #415 の結論のとおり。
- 書き込み先は `/tmp` 配下のみ。checkout 内を指定すると拒否（未レビューの成果物として commit される事故を塞ぐ）。
- `filename` は URL 末尾セグメントが `default.docx` のような汎用名になるため。表示名はコメント本文側にしか無い。

`probe` は削除していない（#415 の指示どおり、`fetch_attachment` が安定した後の子で）。`docs/design-doc` スキル・`generate.mjs`・`publish_draft`・orphan ブランチには触れていない。

## 実測（この PR のコードを source から動かして実 URL に対して実行）

`/tmp/atomaton-workspace/measure-fetch-attachment.ts` から `attachmentUrlFrom` → `attachmentPathFor` → `downloadAttachment`（= ツール handler と同じ経路）を呼んだ結果:

```
[atomaton-attachments] fetch_attachment https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34306035/default.docx
  -> /tmp/atomaton-workspace/attachments/default.docx
[atomaton-attachments] fetch_attachment 5867214B
  application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document in 426ms
{
  "path": "/tmp/atomaton-workspace/attachments/default.docx",
  "bytes": 5867214,
  "content_type": "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document",
  "source_url": "https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34306035/default.docx",
  "head_hex": "504b030414000808",
  "head_ascii": "PK"
}
refused: https://example.com/a.docx is not an attachment this tool fetches. It reads
  `https://github.com/user-attachments/files/<id>/<name>` and
  `https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/...`, and refuses every other host: ...
```

- 保存先の先頭は `504b0304` = `PK\x03\x04`（docx の zip 実体）。#415 が probe read で観測した `head_hex` と一致。
- allowlist 外の URL は拒否され、メッセージが「何を読むツールか」を名指しする。
- 測ったファイルは 5.6MB で workspace の上限を圧迫するので、記録後に削除済み（再取得は 0.4 秒）。

## 検証

- `bun run typecheck` — exit 0。
- `bun run test` — **2189 pass / 0 fail**（170 files）。追加前は 2180 だったので +9。
- 新規 `tests/contract/attachments-fetch.test.ts`（9 tests）:
  - allowlist: 実 URL・`private-user-images` は通し、`example.com`、`github.com/user/repo/raw/...`（リポジトリのファイルであって chat 添付ではない）、lookalike ホスト、`http:` を拒否。
  - ローカル `Bun.serve` で 302 → 実体を返し、**同一呼び出しで追跡**され、保存されたバイトが最終レスポンスのもの（先頭 `PK`）であること。
  - そのサーバーが受けた全リクエストに `Authorization` が無いこと。
  - 26MB を stream する応答（content-length 無し）で上限に当たり、**ファイルが書かれない**こと。
  - `filename` 指定 / URL 末尾セグメント / `dir` 指定、`/tmp` 外とパス形の filename の拒否、schema 形状。
- `src/entrypoints/tools/defaults.yaml` の attachments description、`docs/tools/reference.md` と `src/content/README.md` の同サーバー行に `fetch_attachment` を足した（同じ文が 3 か所にあるため）。

## 未測定として残ること

private リポジトリの添付を anon で読めるか。この PR はトークンを送らないので、404 のときに「無い」と「見えない」を区別できない — エラーメッセージがそう書く形にしてある。`ghs_` × private asset の測定は #415 が「別の測定で行うのが正しい場所」と記録しているので、ここでは測っていない。

---

Wait — PR head is atomaton/issue-418, base is atomaton/issue-12. So the merge commit 7f6ce01 would be created on atomaton/issue-12 (the base), not on issue-418.

Hmm, but the compare showed merge_base_commit for main...7f6ce01 is 7f6ce01, meaning 7f6ce01 IS an ancestor of main. So it's in main.

But the branch atomaton/issue-418's tip is 7f6ce01? That's odd — it means the branch atomaton/issue-418 points at the merge commit. That can happen if... actually GitHub's merge for a stacked PR: merging PR #419 into atomaton/issue-12 creates merge commit 7f6ce01 on atomaton/issue-12. Then how does atomaton/issue-418 point at it?

Wait — matching-refs gave `refs/heads/atomaton/issue-418` = 7f6ce012. And compare(main...7f6ce012) said merge_base_commit = 7f6ce012, meaning 7f6ce012 is an ancestor of main — i.e., it's contained in main. Hmm, actually compare base=main, head=7f6ce01. merge_base = 7f6ce01 means 7f6ce01 is reachable from main. Yes so it's in main.

So atomaton/issue-418 points at a commit already in main. Under my new rule: tip=7f6ce01, PR #419 head.sha=87e54a9 ≠ tip → "unmerged" → resume atomaton/issue-418. But its work IS delivered (it's in main). So resuming it is wrong-ish but is it harmful?

Actually — that's exactly the old behavior too! The old rule asked "did a PR from this branch merge" → yes → merged → don't resume. My new rule says "tip != landed sha" → unmerged → resume. So for #418, my change *regresses* from "don't resume (correct)" to "resume" (incorrect).

But wait. Is resuming harmful? The run would check out atomaton/issue-418, which is at a commit in main. Then create_pr would compare head=atomaton/issue-418 vs base=main. Since the tip is an ancestor of main... gh pr create would fail with "No commits between main and atomaton/issue-418".

Hmm. But that branch is stale anyway — issue #418 is likely closed. Actually let's think about when resolve_issue_branch runs: on a run for issue #418. If the issue is closed, no run. So the practical impact is limited.

But more importantly, there's a real regression class: every *stacked child* branch. When a child PR merges into its parent's branch, GitHub creates a merge commit on the PARENT's branch (base). But wait — with `--merge` into base atomaton/issue-12, the merge commit goes on atomaton/issue-12. So atomaton/issue-418's tip would stay at the push commit.

Unless... the branch was later pushed to again. Hmm, actually GitHub's `gh pr merge` on a stacked PR: does the head branch get updated? No.

So why does atomaton/issue-418 = 7f6ce01? Let me reconsider: maybe merge_commit_sha is not where it says. Actually, maybe the branch atomaton/issue-418 was used as the base for *another* PR (a child of #418), and merges created commits on it. #418 is a parent issue ("fetch_attachment" is one child). And issue-418's head is 87e54a9 which then merged into issue-12. Hmm but then issue-418's tip should be 87e54a9.

Hold on — actually re-read: PR #419 baseRefName = "atomaton/issue-12", headRefName = "atomaton/issue-418". And after merge, is atomaton/issue-418 still at 87e54a9? matching-refs says 7f6ce01. Contradiction unless something advanced it.

Wait — maybe I mis-assigned. Let me re-check: matching-refs/heads/atomaton listed issue-418 = 7f6ce01206d8ba1d17e2090777bfac1c17be5853. And PR #419's merge_commit_sha = 7f6ce01206d8ba1d17e2090777bfac1c17be5853. So the branch atomaton/issue-418 points AT the merge commit of PR #419, which merged into atomaton/issue-12.

That's strange but possible: GitHub DOES update... no. Hmm, actually maybe the base of #419 was later... 

OK. Whatever the mechanism, the empirical fact is: a branch exists whose tip is a commit already contained in main, and whose PR head.sha differs from that tip. Under my rule it reads "unmerged" and resumes it. That's a false "resume", whose consequence is: the run checks out that branch, and later `create_pr` refuses because there are no commits between. That's a worse failure than the old "start on base".

But actually, is that a real scenario for a *live* issue? The branch exists for issues 12, 164, 418. Those issues' branches are stale leftovers. If a new run on issue #418 happened, my change would resume. Old code: PR from issue-418 merged → merged → stay on base. So yes, a regression.

Hmm, but how important? Let me think about what the RIGHT rule is.

The real question is: "does this branch's work still need delivering?" The robust answer is: is the tip contained in the base? But the module's comment explicitly rejects ancestry because squash/rebase rewriting breaks it — and this repo uses merge commits only.

Better: the tip is delivered if it is the head.sha of a merged PR, OR it is the merge_commit_sha of a merged PR, OR ... Actually the cleanest: the branch's tip is "delivered" when a merged pull request FROM this branch either had this sha as its head (nothing added since) or landed this sha (its merge commit equals the tip — which for a stacked child means the tip is a merge commit that is already in the base).

Hmm, but that second condition is odd for the parent branch case: issue-441's tip d9894f0 was... let me check: is d9894f0 a merge_commit_sha of some merged PR? PRs #463/#468/#469 merged as merge commits on atomaton/issue-441. Those merge commits would be on atomaton/issue-441, and their merge_commit_sha would be something. The tip d9894f0 is the last of those. So under "tip == merge_commit_sha of a merged PR from this branch" → d9894f0 would be delivered?! That would break the fix!

Unless the merged-PR query with head= only returns PRs whose head branch is atomaton/issue-441... #463/#468/#469 had head branches atomaton/issue-460/461/462, and base atomaton/issue-441. So they don't appear in head=owner:atomaton/issue-441. Good.

So for atomaton/issue-418: which merged PR has merge_commit_sha = 7f6ce01? PR #419 — whose head IS atomaton/issue-418. So it matches "a merged PR from this branch landed this very commit".

But then for issue-441, tip d9894f0 = merge commit of #469, whose head was atomaton/issue-462 ≠ issue-441. So not matched. 

Hmm, but this is getting subtle and I'm reasoning about a coincidence of two shapes. Let me think about why issue-418's tip is the merge commit at all.

OH. I bet I understand now: `deleteMergedBranch(headRefName)` — merge_pr deletes the merged branch. But PR #419 was merged... base atomaton/issue-12. Hmm.

Alternatively: maybe when the parent's branch (issue-12) then later merged into main, and... no, that doesn't move issue-418.

Actually, maybe git's behavior: git push to atomaton/issue-418 was not the mechanism. Let me instead just accept it as an observed fact and consider whether my rule is right.

Let me step back and think about the actual correctness requirement rather than reverse-engineering one stale branch.

The question the code must answer: "should this run check out this branch, i.e. does it hold work that has not reached the base?"

Old answer: "has any PR from this branch merged?" — fails when the branch advanced past the merged PR's head (#441 case).

My answer: "is the branch's tip the head sha of a merged PR?" — fails when the branch's tip advanced for a reason other than receiving new work (the #418 case), OR when the PR was merged with a merge commit and the branch tip... hmm.

Honestly, a more robust criterion that covers both: the tip is delivered if a merged PR from this branch exists whose head.sha == tip OR whose merge_commit_sha == tip (because that means the tip itself is the commit that landed, so nothing newer exists). For #441: PR #455 head 1f20827, merge_commit_sha = ? Let me get it — if it's not d9894f0, the fix holds.

For #418: merge_commit_sha 7f6ce01 == tip, so delivered → don't resume (correct, old behavior preserved).

That seems principled: "a merged PR from this branch landed this exact commit" means the branch has nothing newer than what landed.

Let me check PR #455's merge_commit_sha to make sure it isn't d9894f0.

Actually, careful — PR #455 was merged into main (base main per earlier get_pr: baseRefName "main"). Its merge commit would be on main. d9894f0 is the tip of atomaton/issue-441 which is NOT in main (it was merged later via #477 into main at f2c5941). So merge_commit_sha of #455 ≠ d9894f0. Good.

So the refined rule: merged if a merged PR from this branch has head.sha == tip OR merge_commit_sha == tip.

Both are "this exact commit is what a pull request landed". That's actually consistent with the doc sentence I wrote: "A branch is merged when the commit it points at now is one a pull request landed." head.sha is the commit as proposed; merge_commit_sha is the commit as landed. Both are the same commit when the merge was fast-forwarded... whatever.

This is the better fix and it's a real bug in what merged. {"body": "## Why this follows #478

#478 made "merged" mean *the commit this branch points at now is one a landing produced*, which fixed what #476 reported: `atomaton/issue-441` sat at `d9894f0` with three undelivered child merges and read as merged, so the parent's aggregation run started on `main` and `create_pr` refused with head == base.

But that change asked only about `head.sha`, and a landing produces **two** commits.

## The shape it gets wrong

A child's pull request merges **into** its parent's branch. GitHub therefore creates the merge commit **on that branch**, and it becomes the parent's tip — nobody's `head.sha`, but exactly the child's `merge_commit_sha`.

Real data, from this run:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `atomaton/issue-418` tip | `7f6ce012…` |
| PR #419 `head.sha` | `87e54a9b…` |
| PR #419 `merge_commit_sha` | `7f6ce012…` ← **the tip** |
| `compare(main...7f6ce012)` `merge_base_commit.sha` | `7f6ce012…` ← **already in main** |

So #418's children have all merged and its work is in `main`, and the rule reads it as undelivered.

## What that costs

The same dead end as #476, reached from the opposite side:

1. `headBranchMerged` answers unmerged (`87e54a9 ≠ 7f6ce012`)
2. `resolve_issue_branch` writes `branch=atomaton/issue-418`
3. the workflow checks it out and sets `BRANCH=atomaton/issue-418`
4. `create_pr` finds nothing between it and the base, so there is no pull request to open

A run spent on a branch with nothing left to deliver, and the aggregation still does not land.

## The fix

`headBranchMerged` asks whether the tip is **either** commit a landing of this branch produced:

```ts
return parsed.some(
  (pr) => Boolean(pr.merged_at) && (pr.head?.sha === tip || pr.merge_commit_sha === tip),
);
```

Both comparisons sit in one answer because they are one question. This is not a second rule bolted on — it is the same rule, with the second half of what "a landing" means.

The `unmerged`-on-failure direction from #478 is unchanged, and the #476 case still behaves: real #441 values (`d9894f0` vs PR #455 head `1f20827`) give `branch="atomaton/issue-441"`, `resuming`.

## Verification

- `scan_secrets` / `typecheck` / `synth` — all exit 0
- `bun run test` — **2225 pass, 0 fail** (6703 expect(), 172 files)
- `bun test src/adapters/adapters.test.ts src/entrypoints/machinery/resolve_issue_branch.test.ts` — 63 pass

Two new regression tests, at both levels — the adapter (`a branch whose tip is the merge commit a pull request created is merged`) and the script the workflow step reads (`a branch whose tip is the merge commit a pull request created is not resumed`). **Both confirmed red with the `merge_commit_sha` comparison removed, green with it.** The four #476/#478 tests stay green throughout.

## How this was found, and the lesson

By running the merged rule against the repository's **real** branch tips and each branch's real merged `head.sha`, rather than only against the fixture that reproduces #476. #476's own fixture passes either way; the defect is only visible against a branch something else merges into.

`docs/work/how-it-works/the-branch-a-run-commits-to.md` states both commits, and `OwnedBranch.merged`'s contract is reworded to match.

## Note for the reviewer

The deployed copy in `.github/atomaton-runtime/scripts/resolve_issue_branch.ts` still carries the **pre-#478** rule, because it is the last release (`v0.21.58`) applied by self-deploy, not by a work PR. That is expected and is not this PR's concern; it becomes current on the next release. No version bump here.
